Hi Samir —

Following our call today I attached a draft mutual action plan (MAP_v2.xlsx) focused on the cost checks you asked for: tokens-per-call sensitivity, caching hit-rate assumptions, and batching profiles during peak vs baseline traffic. High level notes in the doc; summary below so we have the same frame for the evaluation plan and timeline.

Quick summary (high level):
- Acceptance criteria: max cost per active-user request <= $0.0035 (tokens/$ target) and P99 latency <= 450ms for 95% of traffic.
- Baseline assumptions (we used your sample): 2.1k tokens/session average, 18% prefix reuse (cacheable), target cache hit-rate 35% for steady state, burst batch size target 8 (continuous batching), 100 qps steady.
- Eval plan: two-week seeded run using our Hosted API + Dedicated capacity for the final week to simulate production concurrency. Run includes 3 test sets: 1) short prompt set (avg 400 tokens), 2) long clinical note drafts (avg 3.8k tokens), 3) mixed traffic reflective of your session distribution.
- Milestones & timeline:
  * Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP and traffic slices + access to sample prod logs (you to share by Tue)
  * Week 1: run synthetic evals and prefetch/kv cache pilot (Redwood infra)
  * Week 2: 7-day seeded production-like run; cost measurement & ops tuning
  * Week 3: readout, finalize preferred config + pricing proposal
  * Target close: end of Week 4 (we can accelerate if procurement is ready)

Open asks for you:
1) Can you share a 48h anonymized traffic sample and the vendor MD table by Tue? (attached a stub prod_traffic_sample.csv we discussed)
2) Which latency/throughput SLA matters most to procurement (P95 vs P99)?
3) Any internal quota gating we should know (max monthly tokens or seat-based limits)?

I'll flag Neha and Karthik for the technical cost assumptions so we can produce the pricing_proposal.pdf and an ops checklist for the eval.

Thanks — I kept the MAP intentionally short so we can iterate quickly.

Thanks — reviewed the sample and the MAP. A few technical clarifications and proposed adjustments to the cost model before we finalize pricing: 

- Tokens per interaction: the sample mixes short and long sessions. For cost sensitivity we should model three buckets (S/M/L) with weights 52/30/18 from your extract. I'll include per-token spend at the model/quantization levels (FP16 vs 4-bit quant) — 4-bit reduces unit cost ~2.3x in our benchmarks but increases decode latency ~10% in long sequences.
- Caching: define two cache layers: prefix-level reuse (what you saw in the initial dialogs) and KV cache for multi-step composition. Use a conservative 30% overall hit-rate for the baseline run and model an upside 45% optimistic scenario. Please confirm if the 18% prefix reuse you mentioned is normalized across session types or only for templated dialogs.
- Batching: our continuous batching engine will batch at arrival; assume effective batch sizes of 1.6 in low-QPS windows and 7.8 at peak with a 25ms queuing window. If you need stricter P95, we can lower the queuing window (reduces batch size and increases cost).
- Prefetch/pinned-cache: for the clinical note summarization flow we can prefetch likely completions and save ~12-18% token spend when applied selectively. This requires ~2 days to integrate test hooks in your staging environment.

Proposed eval plan (detailed):
- Step A (48-72h): synthetic load tests with three buckets; measure tokens-per-input, latency distributions, and cache hit traces.
- Step B (4-7d): seeded run at 1x production QPS on Hosted API, capture token breakdown and ops flags.
- Step C (optional accelerated pilot): Dedicated capacity week with fixed reserved nodes to simulate tail behavior (we can compress to 4 days if procurement signs pilot SLA).

Deliverables from Redwood after the run: cost-sensitivity spreadsheet (tokens/$ by model variant), a short ops playbook (batching/cache knobs), and a pricing_proposal.pdf. I'll attach the eval test sets we plan to use.
